\subsection{Class-AB Amplifier}\label{ss:ampab}

One cell, \texttt{anatop\_tia\_amp\_ab} (34 transistors; schematic, symbol, layout and
extracted views), serves as both amplifiers of a potentiostat channel: the
transimpedance amplifier A2 (Section~\ref{sss:ampab-tia}) and the control amplifier A1
(Section~\ref{sss:ampab-ctrl}). The cell name records its first application; the device
is role-independent and the two roles differ only in the network around it. All data in
this section is schematic-level, with no extracted parasitics.

The topology is drawn in Figure~\ref{fig:tiaampab-topology}. A complementary
rail-to-rail input stage places an NMOS and a PMOS pair in parallel, both active at the
\SI{1.25}{\volt} common mode used throughout this section; the two pairs fold into a
cascode summing stage, which drives a class-AB output stage whose two output devices are
both actively driven. Cascode (Ahuja) compensation is taken from the common source node
of the PMOS cascodes, \texttt{C1}, and of the NMOS cascodes, \texttt{C2}. Both nodes are
brought out as pins and returned to the output by one \SI{500}{\femto\farad} capacitor
each, outside the cell, so compensation is set per application without editing the cell.

Bias comes from the local bias generator of Section~\ref{ss:biasgen-local} over the
global cascode rails, at trim code \texttt{BiasAdj}~=~37 throughout this section.

The device-level characterisation below is taken at a \SI{2.5}{\volt} supply into a
\SI{5}{\pico\farad} load on three benches: the unity-feedback bench of
Figure~\ref{fig:tb-unityfb}, an open-loop bench with the input offset nulled before
measurement, and a swept-load drive bench. Coverage is five corner points --- the
typical statistical point at nominal and \SI{37}{\celsius}, and the ff, fs, sf and ss
skew corners at \SI{25}{\celsius}, uniform across every test of this bench --- and a
200-sample Monte Carlo run varying process and mismatch together at \SI{37}{\celsius}.
